Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA, Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO.) 36 S. 2010 SEP 2 s 2010 MR. BENJAMIN RAMOS 36 Tamblot St. Barangay Masagana Project 4, Quezon City Dear Mr. Ramos: This has reference to your letter-inquiry as to whether or not the construction of a Barangay Hall in an open space belonging to and owned by the Quezon City Government is legal. Further, you inquired that if such is indeed legal, will the construction of said Barangay Hall in an open space be allowed even without a construction or building permit. Appended to your letter is a photocopy of Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) No. RT- 21710 said to be registered in the name of the Quezon City Government covering the supposed lot/open space, bearing an annotation which reads: "No portion of the property herein delineated as Rd. alley and open space shall be closed or otherwise disposed of without the approval of the NHA, as per PD-957. " Assuming that the barangay hall you mentioned is being constructed on the land covered by the TCT you have attached, and no NHA approval had been secured, then no other conclusion can be had except that the construction is violative of the TCT anno_tation. Moreover, we cite the case of United BF Homeowners Association Inc. vs. The Barangay Chairman and the Sangguniang Barangay of BF Homes Paranaque, G.R.No. 140092, 08 September 2006, wherein the Supreme Court held that: "Before anything else, lest the Court be accused of giving its imprimatur to an illegal act, it should be pointed out that the construction Of the hall in the "open space" was prohibited by law. The second paragraph of Section 31 of PD 957, as amended by PD 1216, categorically provides: Section 31. Roads, Alleys, Sidewalks and Open Spaces. — x x x Open spaces shall be non-alienable public lands, and non- buildable. x x x Thus, no structure or edifice should have been built on the old basketball court as it was an area declared and reserved by law as an "open space" in BF Homes Subdivision. " (emphasis supplied)

Thus, applying the case law to your query, the on-going construction of the Barangay Hall in the open space located at Project 4, Quirino District, Quezon City is prohibited. The issue on whether the same has a building permit or not is insignificant because the act of building the barangay hall itself is a prohibited act. No valid or legal act can proceed nor arise from an illegitimate or illegal act. As to the liabilities of the persons or officials involved, we regret to inform you that it is beyond this Department's duty to advice particular offenses that may be filed against erring officials. We hope that we have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Very truly yours, ATTY. JESUS B. DP9UE IV Director 11B/ LS:55/
